custody_model: Centralized app-hosted staking. Current first-party terms state that Revolut uses third-party validators or partners to stake cryptoassets on the user's behalf, that the staked cryptoassets are not transferred to the third party, and that Revolut continues holding them on the user's behalf while the user remains beneficial owner. Legal-title, safeguarding and entity treatment can vary by jurisdiction and are not universalized.
yield_source: Proof-of-stake network or validator rewards associated with supported cryptoassets, distributed to customers net of applicable third-party and/or Revolut commissions under the relevant jurisdiction and product terms.
risk_notes: Risks include token-price volatility, validator performance, slashing that may reduce rewards or principal, token-specific warm-up and lock-up/unbonding periods, network or protocol failures, platform/custody exposure, variable/non-guaranteed rewards and jurisdiction-specific fee/regulatory treatment. Beneficial ownership does not itself establish universal legal segregation or insolvency protection.
